newsitem.title: USA: Forcenergy sees well boosting reserves.
newsitem.headline: Forcenergy sees well boosting reserves.

text.p: Forcenergy Inc said Tuesday its previously announced Gulf of Mexico exploratory well at High Island A-470 has encountered another pay sand, bringing the total net feet of pay encountered in the well to about 450.
The company said it anticipates some 22.0 billion cubic fet equivalent of proven reserves have been added with this well.

It said an exploratory well drilled on one of Forcenergy's Gulf of Mexico lease blocks by another operator under a farm-out agreement. The well is currently producing about 25 million cubic feet of gas daily.

The Forcenergy AB affiliate said it will convert its existing 8.33 percent overriding royalty to a 30 percent working interest position upon the well achieving payout. Forcenergy estimates that significant proven reserves are associated with the discovery.

It said two successful development wells have been drilled in the company's Trading Bay Field in Alaska's Cook Inlet resulting in net proven reserves of about 500,000 barrels of oil. As a result of the success of these two wells, Forcenergy expects additional wells may be drilled which could add up to one million barrels of oil to Forcenergy's interest.

In Australia, Forcenergy has participated in the drilling of a successful exploratory well which is expected to produce approximately 120 barrels daily net to the company's interest. Forcenergy estimates that, net to its interest, about 250,000 barrels of oil are associated with the discovery.
